A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KnowledgeSmith and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Existing content can be matched across the conference reformatting and appendix renumbering; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing, unlearning, robustness, and representation-analysis experiments across multiple LLMs, with numerical results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments with alternative intervention methods and sequential updates in Appendices E and F.

M1.justification: The constrained-optimization framework, positive/preservation probes, and KG-to-question generation pipeline are unchanged. The additional intervention algorithms and sequential tests extend evaluation without revising the proposed framework.

E1.justification: The four KG domains and MMLU/TruthfulQA coverage remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a five-fact sequential-update scenario, extending the earlier isolated-intervention setting to models carrying a history of previous updates. Appendix E uses the existing domains.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds evaluated MEND editing and gradient-ascent unlearning using the TOFU framework, with results across four subjects, three hierarchy levels, and five training sizes in Tables 8–9. This substantially broadens the original AlphaEdit/ReLearn comparison and retained LoRA analysis; MEND was previously cited but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces cumulative testing after one through five interventions, reassessing earlier facts using Qwen3-14B, LLaMA3-8B, and Gemma-7B. Existing single-intervention settings, metrics, and the 1–10,000-example training-size grid remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Two substantive analyses are added: testing whether hierarchical propagation patterns depend on the intervention algorithm in Appendix E, and examining cumulative interference and retention across sequential updates in Appendix F. Existing robustness, stress-testing, LoRA, and representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same means and standard deviations across data scales. The added tables introduce no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Tables 8–11 add hierarchical results for alternative methods and sequential-update trajectories. Table 10 reports editing Fact 1 accuracy changing from 55.0% to 53.5% across five updates; Table 11 reports unlearning Fact 1 accuracy changing from 54.2% to 27.2%. Existing main results and v1 Tables 8–15, renumbered 12–19, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation in Equations 1–3, CCR/RR definitions in Equations 4–5, and SVD-based mathematical discussion are retained. The added appendices provide empirical observations and interpretations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and substantive conclusion retain the same framework, benchmark-generation, and knowledge-updating claims. Additional appendix evidence does not revise these stated main contributions; the deleted concluding paragraph concerns future research.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly attributes propagation asymmetry to KG structure independently of the intervention algorithm. Appendix F interprets sequential results as showing robust, localized editing and inherently more disruptive unlearning. This materially extends the interpretation without explaining its relationship to the retained claims that unlearning better preserves stability and robustness. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Generation prompts and validation instructions, software-stack disclosures, H100 timing estimates, and code/data-release statements are retained. The added experiments identify methods, models, and evaluation schedules but supply no new implementation instructions or hyperparameters.

R1.justification: v3 adds Maini et al. (2024), TOFU, to support the new unlearning experiment. MEND's reference already appeared in v1. The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include short pointers to new Appendices E/F, appendix renumbering, removal of the concluding future-work paragraph, minor wording edits, and changing the displayed author name from Yixuan Li to Sharon Li.

P2.justification: The paper adopts an ICLR layout with different margins, headings, typography, and display placement. Four new tables are added. Figure 7 changes from large vertically stacked editing/unlearning grids to much smaller side-by-side panels, substantially reducing legibility; existing appendix tables are also resized and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Appendices E/F broaden method coverage and address previously untested sequential updates. However, the sequential tables do not explain model-specific results or aggregation, and the target of unlearning accuracy is insufficiently specified. Their claim of inherently greater disruption is not reconciled with the retained stability conclusions. Figure 7 also becomes substantially harder to read. These reporting and interpretation problems make the added evidence's value uncertain, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
